title: Protect host audio stream lifetimes before raw SDK submission
goal: Provide original bounded host owner/session admission so closed audio tokens cannot reach a reused raw SDK stream, without revising the SDK ABI or admitting guest services.
acceptance: Define a standalone C++20 eight-stream ownership gate with opaque instance/session-bound tokens and explicit nonzero host owner IDs; reject invalid, closed, moved, foreign-instance and wrong-owner commands before any backend call, including raw-ID reuse

Serialize public operations on the creating host thread; SDK callbacks only record bounded per-binding credits through detached lifetime state, never reenter a backend or call arbitrary clients. Old callbacks cannot credit a replacement, and exhaustion fails diagnostically without wrapping identifiers/counters

Use an explicit narrow backend port, preserve backend refusal/errors and earlier valid owners on ordinary failure, bound frame spans to the established original host PCM shape, and release owned streams on close/owner-close/shutdown without per-submit ownership allocations or PCM copies

Prove admission against the actual unchanged approved SDK in explicit timer and SDL dummy modes: retain the raw stale-ID baseline, reject that stale host token before SDK Submit, and show the replacement/other owner still progresses with correct cleanup

Keep SDK-specific glue in the diagnostic lane; no shared SDK/profile, input, allocation, startup, existing runtime interface, guest ABI, profile authentication or title playback change. Any production integration or broader interface change requires a separate agreed task
validation: Run original positive/negative native contracts on Windows/Linux, including partial-open/submit failure, active raw-ID collision, close/reopen, owner/instance isolation, delayed callbacks, bounded exhaustion, frame bounds and wrong-thread calls; distinguish model faults from actual SDK observations

Run supported public-core and SDK-facing host sanitizers, actual SDK isolated/repeated/reordered cases, strict nonce/library/result controls and resource recovery; identify uninstrumented library coverage and physical/title checks not run

Measure token admission/submission/callback progress over at least three independent comparable processes, retain tails and correctness work, run public checks, and publish exact source/compiler/package/library/binary identities with material limits
size: bounded original host lifetime gate plus actual-SDK diagnostic bridge; no shared ABI repair or title binding
evidence: docs/engine/audio-streams.md records the standalone C++20 eight-stream host gate, backend/thread/destruction preconditions, exact evidence identities, results, performance and production handoff; original source only in the reserved paths

Opaque instance/session tokens reject default, moved, foreign, stale and wrong-owner commands before backend calls. Closing/owner-close/shutdown invalidates before release; detached serialized callback counters cannot credit replacement state. Small binding/frame budgets exercise exhaustion without wrapping

Nine model groups pass on Windows/MSVC, Windows MSVC ASan and Linux/GCC ASan/UBSan, including ordinary open/submit rollback, duplicate/zero raw IDs fail-closed without closing earlier owners, delayed callback copies, wrong-thread operations, frame bounds, reentry and deterministic cleanup. These injected faults are synthetic, not SDK playback evidence

Actual unchanged approved SDK bridge passes four Windows/Linux native/host-sanitizer profiles: 128 process checks including 16 expected wrong-result/incomplete controls. Three isolated repeats and both case orders cover timer and six-channel SDL dummy modes, retained raw-ID aliasing, valid replacement/other-owner progress, actual queue refusal/recovery, 32-cycle lifetimes and recovered streams/queues/SDK-tracked threads/SDL state

Forty ordinary raw reuse observations remain unsafe at raw ID 2; 1360 ordinary stale host commands are rejected before another SDK Submit. MW3-061 original failing receipts are retained; this fixes host admission, not the SDK raw-ID ABI or guest/title audio

Eight Python evidence-guard tests reject malformed/stale/typed/partial/duplicate results, fallback devices, wrong SDK call counts and failed controls; an actual owned child times out after plausible output. Compiler/package/source/binary/loaded-library/log/artifact hashes verified before/after; host core/bridge instrumented, SDK/SDL internals uninstrumented

Three independent model processes per OS discard 256 warmup calls then measure 4096 batches of 64 submits, retaining tails and checking all credits with zero measured submit allocations. Batch-averaged per-run medians 9.375 ns Windows and 7.203125-11.765625 ns Linux are synthetic trivial-backend costs only. Actual SDK 160-call/32-cycle per-process timings and refusal tails are separately published without a gameplay or audible-latency claim

Windows public check.py Release passes 203 Python tests/eight skips plus parser CTest 1/1; Linux Release --sanitizers passes 203 tests/two Windows-only skips plus parser 1/1. No shared input/startup/allocation/SDK/interface changes, game bytes, SDKs or private logs committed. Self-review only; production adapter/owner mapping, guest admission, physical output and MW3-082 remain separate agreed work
